question: Where is the model-scope gradient error, and is it distributed or located?
answer: LOCATED, entirely. `diffusion_module.diffusion_transformer` carries 43.6221 % of the mass at rel_L2 8.1943 against float64 with a norm ratio of 8.5625 and cosine 0.4187. Remove that one section and the remaining 48.5347 % of mass over 451 tensors reads 0.0675 against float64 -- BELOW upstream's own bf16 training step, which is 0.0753 from the same float64 -- and 0.1123 against upstream's own bf16, which is 1.07x the A26 reachable bar. The campaign's headline 5.6379 is one section.
the_open_question: This arm's diffusion capture is /home/ttuser/of3t_f64softmax/device_grads_043all_shipped.pt. `of3t-ditref` (concluded, GO) re-measured the diffusion module on a DIFFERENT capture, /home/ttuser/of3t_softgrad/diffcap043, with the 0.4.3 reference tree resolved and read back in-process, and got 0.0934424638 vs float64 over 547 tensors and 0.5865x upstream 0.4.3's own bf16. Those are different captures and different tensor sets, so they do not formally contradict -- but the model-scope number the charter reads has never been re-taken since that repair, and it is the ONLY thing standing between this campaign and a gradient-confidence statement. Nothing else at model scope is above the reachable bar by more than 1.07x.
note: A norm ratio of 8.5625 with cosine 0.4187 is not a precision signature. Precision error shrinks a cosine toward 1 and leaves the norm near 1; this is a different function or a different scale, which is also why no softmax or dtype lever has moved it.
